description: What is running: windows (only the primary is inspected), size, scale, colour scheme, focus, clock, reload generation and last reload, animations under way (wait for them after a click), and this connection's capabilities. `after_reload` with `wait_ms` waits for a reload.

input_schema.description: What `app_status` may be asked besides the state itself.

after_reload.description:
Wait until the reload generation is greater than this, or a reload
fails, up to `wait_ms`.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for a reload, in milliseconds (at most 30000).

input_schema.title: StatusArgs

name: app_status

description: Outline of what the app shows: one line per item with role, name, value, state and a reference (`e12`) to use in other tools. Start here. `root` limits it to one subtree, `depth` to some levels; a cut outline gives a `cursor` for the next part; `since` lists only what changed.

Include.description: What a snapshot line shows beyond role, name, value and state.

oneOf.description: ` at=x,y size=WxH`, in window coordinates.
` type=Rectangle`: the QML type.
` desc="…"`: the accessible description.

cursor.description:
The `next_cursor` of a cut outline: gives its next part. Not
combined with `root`, `depth`, `include` or `since`.

depth.description:
How many levels below the first line are listed. What is deeper is
counted, not listed.

image.description: Also attach a PNG of the window.

max_nodes.description: Cut the outline after this many items (default and limit 400).

pointer.description:
`true`: from now on also list the shown items that take the pointer
and have no accessible role (a `MouseArea`, an item with a
`TapHandler`, a `Flickable`), as `pointer` lines with a reference
that the click and touch tools take. `false`: stop. What the
accessibility tree reports does not change.

root.description:
List only this item and what is below it: a reference (`e12`) or a
locator that matches exactly one item.

since.description: The `epoch` of an earlier snapshot: list only what changed since.

name: app_snapshot

description: Find items by locator: `role=button[name="Save"]`, `text=notes`, `#objectName`, `id=qmlId`, `name~=regex`, `e12`; `a >> b` searches in a, `>> nth=0` picks one; `at=X,Y`: what is drawn at a window point, topmost first. Each match: reference, path, bounds, states. None is not an error.

limit.description: List at most this many matches (default 50, limit 200).

locator.description:
What to look for, e.g. `role=button[name="Save"]`, `text=notes`,
`#objectName`, `role=list >> role=listitem >> nth=0`. `at=X,Y`
lists every item drawn at that point of the window (logical
pixels), topmost first, those with no role too, with the type and
the file and line each was written at.

name: app_find

description: One item in depth: type, id, file and line, geometry, window singletons, properties with where each value is from (assigned, bound at tier 0/1/js, animated, host, default). `all` adds defaults; `dependencies` names a property: its reads, readers, tier; `bindings`: every binding's.

all.description: List every property, including those still at their default.

bindings.description:
Every property of the object that a binding sets, each with what
its binding read, what reads it, and its tier.

dependencies.description:
The name of one property: adds what its binding read when it last
ran, which bindings read it, and the tier its binding runs at.

target.description:
A reference (`e12`) or a locator that matches exactly one item.
`#objectName` and `id=qmlId` also reach items the outline does not
list (not exposed, or not shown), such as the window; `#name` falls
back to the id when no object has that name. `at=X,Y` is the
topmost item drawn at that point of the window, `at=X,Y >> nth=1`
the one under it.

name: app_inspect

description: PNG of the window, or of one item when `target` is given, drawn by the software renderer (works headless). Scaled down so the longest side is at most `max_size` (default and limit 1280 px). Prefer `app_snapshot` for reading text and state: it is smaller and exact.

max_size.description: Longest side of the picture in pixels (default and limit 1280).

target.description:
Picture only this item: a reference or a locator that matches
exactly one item. Without it, the whole window.

name: app_screenshot

description: Recent log lines of the app (`console.log`, warnings, JS errors) with QML file and line when known, oldest first, at most 100. `level` sets the least severe level listed; `since` takes the `next_since` of an earlier answer to get only newer lines.

Level.description: How severe a log line is, least severe first.

level.description:
The least severe level to list: `debug` (default; `console.log`
logs at this level), `info`, `warning` or `critical`.

limit.description: List at most this many lines, the newest ones (default and limit 100).

since.description:
List only lines newer than this sequence number (the `next_since`
of an earlier answer).

name: app_logs

description: Frame work since the inspector attached: frames, time over budget, time per lane, jobs, the owners that took the most time, and a `memory` summary. With `memory` ({`type`, `max`}) it answers where the memory is instead: objects by type, script heap, graph, text, images, scenes.

mappings.description:
Also split what is resident by the mapping it is in: the program,
LLVM, the GPU driver, fonts, other libraries, the allocator's heap,
other anonymous maps (Linux; elsewhere not known). Reads the
process's memory map, a few milliseconds.

max.description:
The most types to list, the most bytes first (default 20, at most
1000). The rest are counted in `types_left_out`.

type.description: Only the objects of this type, by the name `app_objects` gives it.

input_schema.description: `app_metrics`: frame work, or with `memory` where the memory is.

memory.description:
Answer where the application's memory is instead of frame work:
objects by type (about how many bytes), the script heap, the
reactive graph, text caches, images, and per window the scene and
what its renderer keeps. `{}` lists the 20 largest types.

input_schema.title: MetricsArgs

name: app_metrics

description: What does work, like Erlang's observer: threads (state, CPU time, wakeups), Timers, animations, scheduler owners, the supervision tree, the last faults and what took each, and the UI thread's mailboxes (depth, age, refused), even when stuck. `kind` keeps one; `waker`: what will wake it.

oneOf.description: OS threads of the process, the UI thread first.
Running `Timer`s.
Animations under way.

What the frame scheduler charged time to: the application, error
boundaries, the inspector.

The bounded inboxes threads reach the UI thread through. Read
without the UI thread, so a stuck one still shows its inbox.

The supervision tree: the standard supervisors and every live
boundary, under the one around it.

The last faults (at most 32), in `faults`: where each happened and
what took it.

What will wake the UI thread, each with its owner and where it is
declared: running Timers and animations, answers awaited (fetches,
files, media, dialogs), pictures loading, posted messages, and what
listens (file watchers). Only when asked for by name.

kind.description:
List only this kind: `thread`, `timer`, `animation`, `owner`,
`mailbox`, `supervisor`, `fault`, or `waker` (what will wake the UI
thread, listed only when asked for).

mailbox.description:
List only the mailboxes of this name (`application`, `platform`,
`images`, `inspector`, `reload`).

peek.description:
Name the kinds of this many front messages per mailbox (at most 20,
default 0). Never their contents.

name: app_processes

description: Wait until the app changes: frames, drawn passes (`paints`), logs, reloads, `traces`, followed `models`, kept `wakes`, `items` drawn; by name, `rests` (the UI thread slept: `rest`). Answers when a `topics` count differs from `since` (last `counts`), else after `wait_ms`; `settle_ms` gathers a burst.

Since.description: The counts a client was last told; a topic left out is not compared.

items.description: By handle; an item left out is not compared.

Topic.description: What a watch can wait for.

oneOf.description:
Frames the application ran, including ones an inspector's request
asked for.

Passes of the primary window that drew something: the picture
changed.
Lines in the log `app_logs` reads.
Reloads, applied or failed.
Events `app_trace` wrote down.

Changes of the models clients follow (`app_objects`' `model` with
a `holder`).

Wakes of the UI thread kept for `app_frames`' `wakes` that not only
an agent's requests caused.

Times the UI thread went to sleep with a different wake time or
pointer than the last: the answer's `rest` says which.

Passes that changed the picture where one of the watch's `items`
lies.

holder.description:
The name this client gave its traces (`app_trace`'s `holder`),
recording and followed model: they last while it watches.

items.description:
Items to follow, by handle (`@12.3`, as `app_objects` gives them),
at most 16: how many passes changed the picture where each lies,
counted from when it was first watched.

settle_ms.description:
After the first change, wait this much longer so that a burst is
one answer (at most 5000).

since.description:
The `counts` of the last answer. Without them the counts are
answered at once.

topics.description:
Wait for these only: `frames`, `paints`, `logs`, `reloads`,
`traces`, `models`, `wakes`, `rests`, `items`. All but `rests` by
default.

wait_ms.description:
How long to wait at most, in milliseconds (default 10000, at most
3600000).

name: app_watch

description: Every object below `root` (default: the scene's root), with `@handle`, type, id, objectName, depth, bytes; `depth` limits, `next_cursor` pages. `models` lists models; `model` reads rows (`offset`, `limit`), a `holder` follows it. `components` lists loaded ones, `component` (an id) its instances.

component.description:
List the instances of this component (its `component` id in the
list), `limit` from `offset` on.

components.description:
List the components loaded instead of objects: each file, inline
component, delegate and template, with its instances alive and
the bytes they hold.

cursor.description:
The `next_cursor` of a cut answer: the objects after it, below the
same root and to the same depth. Not given with `root` or `depth`.

depth.description: How many levels below the root to list (0 is the root alone).

holder.description:
With `model`: follow the model read, each change moving
`app_watch`'s `models` count while a watch with this `holder` keeps
coming back. With `mark` and `since_mark`: the client's own mark,
kept while its watch does.

limit.description: The most rows or instances to read (default 50, at most 500).

mark.description:
Mark this point: the objects alive now. A later `since_mark` lists
what was made after it and is still alive.

max.description: The most objects to list (default 500, at most 5000).

model.description:
Read the rows of this model, or of the one this view shows: a
`@handle` or a locator.

models.description:
List the application's models instead of objects: each with what
has it, its rows, roles and views.

offset.description: The first row or instance to read (default 0).

root.description:
The object to start at: a `@handle` or a locator. Default: the
scene's root.

since_mark.description:
List what was made since the mark and is still alive, by where
each is declared, with the bytes held. The script collector runs
first.

name: app_objects

description: Trace objects like Erlang's observer: `target` starts one; its signals, changes and end (or only `names`) are written down with the app's time, and with `bindings` each binding run and its cause. A `holder` reads a ring of its own. `since` takes `next_since`; `stop` ends one or all.

bindings.description:
With `target`: also write down each time a binding of the object
runs again, with what it read that changed, how long it took and
whether it gave the value it had.

holder.description:
A name for the client: the trace ends once no `app_watch` with
this `holder` has waited for a while. With `stop` and no
`target`, stops the traces of this holder only.

max.description: The most events to list, oldest first (default 100, at most 500).

names.description:
With `target`: write down only these of its properties and
signals, by name, and its end. All by default.

since.description: The `next_since` of an earlier answer: only what came after it.

stop.description:
Stop tracing `target`, or every object without one. What was
written down stays.

target.description:
Start tracing this object (a reference, locator or `@handle`), or
with `stop`, stop tracing it.

name: app_trace

description: A timeline of every window's frames: `record` starts or stops it; each says what woke it and where its time went, pass by pass. Modes instead: `wakes`, `bindings` (hot bindings, loops), `growth` (instances per component over time), `export` (a trace file). `since` takes `next_since`.

oneOf.description: The most time in all runs, nested runs included.
The most time in all runs less the runs nested in them.
The most runs.
The longest single run.

bindings.description:
The bindings and handlers that ran instead: per each where it is
written, what it writes, its runs, their time and what set them
off; and the binding loops met. `record` starts or stops profiling.

export.description:
Writes the frames, wakes and runs of bindings recorded to a trace
file of this name (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`) in the
application's trace folder, for a trace viewer (Perfetto); the
answer says where.

growth.description:
The instances and bytes of each component over time instead, those
that keep growing first. `record` starts or stops sampling.

holder.description:
A name for the client: with `record`, the recording it asked for
ends once no `app_watch` with this `holder` has waited for a while,
or when it stops it. Others' recordings go on.

last_input.description: With `wakes`: as `wake`, for the latest wake input caused.

max.description: The most frames to list (default 60, at most 600).

record.description:
Start recording (`true`) or stop (`false`). What was recorded
stays until newer frames push it out.

since.description:
The `next_since` of an earlier answer: only the frames after it,
oldest first. Without it, the latest frames.

sort.description:
With `bindings`: the rows by `total` time (default), `own` time
(less what ran nested in them), `runs` or the `longest` run.

wake.description:
With `wakes`: what this wake (its `wake` number) did, in order: the
handlers and bindings that ran, the properties that changed (old
and new), the items laid out, placed and redrawn, and their times.

wakes.description:
The UI thread's wakes instead of the frames: what woke each (input,
a timer, an animation, a message and its kind, the platform) and
what it led to. `record` starts or stops keeping them, apart from
the frames.

name: app_frames

description: The design audit of what the app shows: off-window, covered, cut or faint text, small targets, popups that do not fit, unnamed controls. Each finding: rule, fix, role, locator, file:line, bounds. `matrix`: current, full or points; all is put back. `act`: also press and toggle, running app handlers.

act.description:
Also run the checks that act (focus each stop, press Escape,
toggle controls, open popups): they run the application's own
handlers, whose effects are real. Needs the `input` capability.
Off, the answer's `notChecked` names the codes left out.

matrix.description:
The settings to audit under: `current` (the app as it is, the
default), `full` (also light and dark at normal and high contrast,
larger text and the small window), or points separated by `;`,
each `scheme=light|dark contrast=normal|high font-scale=<n>
size=<w>x<h>|small reduced-motion=true|false`.

max_findings.description:
The most findings to list (default 100, at most 500); the answer
says how many more there were.

root.description:
Only findings about this item and what is inside it: a locator or
a reference, as `app_find` takes. The rest of the window is still
looked at (what covers the item may lie outside it).

rules.description:
Only these rules, by code (`layout-offscreen`) or area (`a11y`,
`color`, `text`, `layout`, `focus`, `motion`, `content`).

touch.description:
Hold what can be pressed to the size a finger needs, not a
pointer's.

name: app_audit

description: Click the item `target` at its centre, or the window's point `at`: a move, a press and a release through a mouse's hit test, so what is on top gets it. `button` is left (default), right or middle; `count` 2 is a double click. Answers once the frame settled, with what changed.

at.description: `[x, y]` in the window's logical pixels; what is on top there gets it. Give this or `target`.

count.description: 1 (default) or 2 for a double click; at most 3.

target.description: A reference (`e12`) or a locator that matches exactly one item. Give this or `at`.

name: app_click

description: Type `text` into the item that has keyboard focus, as key presses with text, like a keyboard. With `target` the item is clicked first. Refused when nothing has focus. Text typed into a field that hides its text is not echoed back. Answers with what changed.

target.description: An item to click first, so that it has keyboard focus.

text.description: The text to type (at most 4000 characters).

name: app_type

description: Press keys: `Enter`, `Tab`, `Escape`, `F5`, a chord such as `Ctrl+A` or `Shift+Tab`; several separated by a space. `repeat` presses them again (up to 100). With `target` the item is clicked first. Goes to the item with keyboard focus. Answers with what changed.

keys.description: Keys: `Enter`, `Ctrl+A`, `Shift+Tab`; several separated by a space.

repeat.description: Press them this many times (default 1, at most 100).

target.description: An item to click first, so that it has keyboard focus.

name: app_press

description: Turn the mouse wheel over `target` (default: the middle of the window) by `dx`, `dy` notches. Negative `dy` shows what is further down. Whatever scrolls under the pointer takes it. Answers with what changed.

dy.description:
Notches away from you, which shows what is further up (default 0);
negative shows what is further down.

target.description:
Where the wheel is turned: a reference or locator. Default: the
middle of the window.

name: app_scroll

description: A finger on `target` (default: the middle of the window): `tap`, or `swipe` by `dx`, `dy` logical pixels. It is a pointer with a touch identity, through the same router as a mouse. `pinch` is not supported yet. Answers with what changed.

dx.description: A swipe moves the finger this far to the right, in logical pixels.

dy.description: A swipe moves the finger this far down.

target.description:
Where the finger is put: a reference or locator. Default: the
middle of the window.

name: app_touch

description: Move the virtual clock by `ms` (at most 60000), firing the timers and animation frames it passes in order. Only for an application on a virtual clock (a test); otherwise unavailable. Answers with what changed.

ms.description: Milliseconds to move the virtual clock (1 to 60000).

name: app_advance

description: Give the window another size in logical pixels, and optionally another `scale`. The application sees it as a resize of the window. A desktop window is resized by its platform and answered once it has the size, or with the size the platform gave instead.

scale.description: Device pixels per logical pixel (0.5 to 4). Unchanged when left out.

name: app_resize

description: Change what the system prefers: `color_scheme` (light or dark), `reduced_motion`, `font_scale` (0.25 to 4). The application reads them as it reads the real ones. Give at least one. Answers with the appearance now and what changed.
name: app_set_appearance

description: Several act steps in one call: `steps` is a list of `{tool, args}` of the input, mutate and eval tools (at most 32). They run in order and stop at the first failure. One difference of the screen is given at the end; each step says what it cost. Every step's capability is needed up front.

tool.description: An input, mutate or eval tool, e.g. `app_click`.

name: app_batch

description: Assign `value` to `property` of `target` as a script would, or bind it to the JS expression `binding` (needs eval too); `keep_binding` covers a binding, `revert` takes the edit back. With `row`, writes that row's role `property` of a model as a delegate does. Answers the value now and before.

binding.description:
A JavaScript expression to bind the property to, naming the
object's properties bare: worked out again whenever what it read
changes. Not with `value` or `revert`.

keep_binding.description:
Cover a binding instead of replacing it, so that `revert` can bring
it back.

revert.description:
Take back what devtools did to the property: the binding it
covered, or the value it had before.

row.description:
Write the role `property` of this row of the model `target` has or
shows, as a delegate writes `model.role`. Only with `value`.

target.description: A reference or a locator that matches exactly one object.

value.description:
A JSON value: a number, text, true or false, null, a list, or an
object for a `var` property. Not with `revert`.

name: app_set_property

description: Call the method `name` of `target` with `args`, or send the signal of that name so its handlers run. Answers with the result and what changed. A method that throws is an `app_faulted` answer with the message.

name.description: A method or signal of the object.

name: app_invoke

description: Reload the changed files now instead of waiting for them to be quiet. Answers `applied` when one was applied since the last `app_reload` answer (a save's own too), `failed` (with the message; the application goes on as it was) or `unchanged`. Needs `--watch`.
name: app_reload

description: Import `module` from `dir`, a directory in the project (or one the application was started with) whose qmldir names it, and reload keeping state; `dir: null` drops the alias. Answers as `app_reload` does, with the generation. Needs `--watch`; `app_status` lists the aliases.

dir.description:
The directory to import it from, relative to the project; null
drops the alias.

module.description: The module, as an import names it: `App.Media`.

name: app_alias

description: Run JavaScript in the context of `target` (default: global scope): its properties are named bare, as in a binding. Stopped after `timeout_ms` (default 1000, at most 10000). The result is written bounded (depth, items, text); it can be as much as the application can do, so it is its own capability.

source.description: The script. Its last expression is the result.

target.description: The object it runs in; default: the global scope.

timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds it may run (default 1000, at most 10000).

name: app_eval
